conventions.convention: Average ranks are assigned to ties before applying Φ⁻¹((r−3/8)/(S+1/4)); the normal-law interface inherits AC.
The empirical quantile is Q_S(u)=x_(ceil(Su)) for 0<u≤1, retaining multiplicities and using no interpolation.
Split chains retain the first and last floor(L/2) observations, discarding the middle observation for odd L. Sample variances use divisor N−1. W=0 returns not estimable; R-hat is not clamped below 1.
The theoretical ESS requires strict stationarity, positive finite marginal variance, absolute autocorrelation summability, and positive τ. It does not assert a CLT.

Multi-chain ESS splits once, uses biased lag autocovariances with divisor N, initial positive and monotone paired sums, odd/even truncation averaging, and the S′log10(S′) cap. A zero split-chain variance or nonpositive estimated τ returns not estimable.
Folding uses absolute deviations from the pooled median, averaging the two central order statistics for an even pooled size; the reported R-hat is the maximum of the rank and folded components.
Tail ESS uses indicators x≤q at the pooled left empirical 5% and 95% quantiles, rank-normalizes those indicators, and returns the smaller ESS.
Quantile MCSE uses Beta(Eα+1,E(1−α)+1) lower quantiles at .16 and .84, maps both through Q_S, and returns half their difference. The interval is an approximation without asserted coverage.
The standard Cauchy law is the density measure 1/(π(1+x²)) relative to Lebesgue measure; its construction assumes Countable Choice.
The eight-schools numerical results are reported empirical observations, distinct from the locally proved finite-array examples.

load_bearing.statement: For M≥2 equal-length scalar chains of length L≥4, split into first and last halves, compute between/within-adjusted autocorrelations, apply positive/monotone paired truncation and odd/even averaging, and return min{S′/τ̂,S′log10(S′)} when the stated variance and positivity checks pass; otherwise return not estimable.
For a nonempty finite pooled collection of real values, assign average ranks r_i to ties and define z_i=Φ⁻¹((r_i−3/8)/(S+1/4)).
For M≥2 equal-length scalar chains with L≥4, split into first and last N=floor(L/2) observations, compute W, B and V̂⁺=(N−1)W/N+B/N, and return sqrt(V̂⁺/W) if W>0; otherwise return not estimable.
Compute split R-hat after pooled Blom normalization of the original draws and of their absolute deviations from the pooled median; return their maximum if both are estimable, otherwise not estimable.
For a strictly stationary real process with 0<σ_h²<∞, absolutely summable autocorrelations, and τ_h=1+2Σρ_h(k)>0, define ESS_h(n)=n/τ_h. This does not assert that a central limit theorem holds.
For S≥1 sorted real draws retaining multiplicities and 0<u≤1, Q_S(u)=x_(ceil(Su)).
The measure μ_C=f dλ with f(x)=1/(π(1+x²)) has total mass one and is the standard Cauchy law.
